summary.title: Does On-Policy Distillation Really Distill? From Noisy Teacher to Self-Improvement

setting_and_object.category: Algorithm (plus a diagnostic analysis of on-policy distillation)

details: On-policy distillation (OPD) has a teacher score student-sampled trajectories that are off-policy for it; the reliability of this supervision, and hence whether gains truly come from knowledge transfer, is unclear.

Diagnostic analysis shows teacher advantages are largely noisy yet the student improves regardless, and that gains concentrate on low log-probability tokens with negative advantages — implying no teacher is needed.
On-Policy Self-Adaptation (OPSA): a supervision-free token-level on-policy RL objective that requires no teacher, verifiable reward, or hint.

Crux: restrict updates to the lowest-log-probability sampled tokens (bottom 20%) and assign them purely negative advantages whose magnitude increases with the token's within-rollout relative entropy, suppressing tail tokens while redistributing mass among competing head tokens at high-entropy fork positions.
Students: Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3.5-9B; teachers for OPD analysis: Qwen3-4B/30B-A3B/235B-A22B-Instruct.
Trained on DAPO-17k questions only (no labels or ground-truth answers), non-thinking mode rollouts.
Evaluation: in-domain AIME24/AIME25/HMMT25 (Avg@32, Pass@32); OOD MBPP+ and GPQA-Diamond.

Noise defined at verifiable answer tokens in \boxed{}: sign of teacher advantage disagreeing with the verifiable reward; measured on 500 DAPO questions with one correct and one incorrect student sample each.
Controlled OPD variants: train on all trajectories vs. only noisy vs. only clean.
Token-selection probes: training only on top-logp tokens with either OPD advantages or random advantages in [-1,1]; signal probes: fixed advantage of -0.5 or +0.2 on the lowest-20% logp tokens.
Entropy-modulation sweep via A_i^dyn = A_fix - (1/4)delta*r_i with delta in {1, 0, -1}, r_i the min-max normalized entropy rank within a rollout.
Loss averaged over the bottom-20% logp tokens with A_i^dyn = -1/2 - (H_i - H_min)/(2(H_max - H_min)).

slime framework with Megatron training and SGLang rollout, 8x H100/H200, lr 1e-6, rollout/global batch 64, 1 sample per prompt, max response 12k tokens; eval with 32 samples, temperature 0.7, 32k max tokens.
No teacher forward passes, so training step time is lower than OPD and GRPO.
Baselines: GRPO (RLVR), TTRL (label-free test-time RL), OPD (Qwen3-4B-Instruct teacher), OPSD (hint-conditioned self-teacher), and NSR (trajectory-level negative-only RLVR).

Ablations: fraction of trained tokens (10/20/30/40%), masking reflective 'fork' positions, thinking-mode inference, token-budget-matched inference control ('wait' continuation) for GRPO/OPD, and OPSA as cold start before GRPO.
Diversity measured by pairwise 4-gram Jaccard distance over 32 samples at prefix lengths 512–4096 and full.

key_findings.finding: OPD teacher supervision on student trajectories is heavily noisy and gets noisier with teacher scale, yet the student's improvement is essentially insensitive to that noise.
key_findings.evidence: Answer-token advantage signs disagree with verifiable rewards for 30.6% of cases with a 4B teacher, 34.7% with 30B-A3B and 50.6% with 235B-A22B (the largest teacher assigns negative advantages to ~97.8% of correct and 96.6% of incorrect answer tokens). Training on all trajectories, only noisy ones, or only clean ones converges to comparable AIME24 Avg@4 in a similar number of steps.

key_findings.finding: OPD's gains stem from applying negative advantages to low-log-probability student tokens rather than from teacher knowledge transfer.
key_findings.evidence: 29.2% of tokens receive exactly zero advantage and 51.7% have |A|<1e-4, concentrated on high-logp tokens; training only on top-logp tokens yields no AIME24 improvement even with random advantages in [-1,1]. Restricting OPD to the bottom-20% logp tokens matches full OPD, and replacing all advantages by a fixed -0.5 gives comparable gains, while a fixed +0.2 causes collapse (response length to near zero, exploding gradient norm).

key_findings.finding: Scaling the negative advantage magnitude positively with token entropy is what turns this mechanism into an improvement over OPD.
key_findings.evidence: With delta=1 (larger negative magnitude at higher-entropy tokens), AIME24 Avg@4 reaches 50.0% vs 35.13% for standard OPD; delta=-1 is unstable between steps 350-450, has persistently higher gradient norms, and ends slightly below the fixed-negative baseline.

key_findings.finding: OPSA, using zero external supervision, outperforms teacher-based and reward-based on-policy baselines and generalizes across model families, scales, and domains.
key_findings.evidence: On Qwen3-1.7B, OPSA reaches 48.85 AIME24 Avg@32 vs base 13.44 (+35.41, +263%) and beats the best baseline by 11.04 Avg@32 and 8.89 Pass@32 averaged over three math benchmarks (GRPO 24.79, OPD 22.15, OPSD 23.58, TTRL 11.81 average Avg@32; NSR 24.13). Gains hold for Qwen3-4B (+38.75 AIME24) and the strong Qwen3.5-9B (+11.46 AIME24, +22.92 HMMT25), plus small OOD gains on MBPP+ and GPQA-Diamond.

key_findings.finding: OPSA works by sharpening low-entropy positions while redistributing mass among head tokens at high-entropy forks, eliciting longer reflective reasoning without collapsing diversity.
key_findings.evidence: Response length grows steadily during training and reflective-token frequency rises, with accuracy correlating positively with length; masking reflective fork positions removes both length and accuracy gains and causes length collapse around step 300. Pass@32 more than doubles on all three benchmarks, the 4-gram Jaccard-distance gap to the base model vanishes at longer prefixes, and OPSA attains higher Pass@32 than GRPO/NSR despite much lower training entropy. Token-budget-matched 'wait' continuations do not improve GRPO (32.81) or OPD (31.67), ruling out length alone.
